question: The mean and standard deviation of 100 observations were calculated as 40 and 5.1 respectively by a student who took 50 instead of 40 for one observation. What is the correct mean and standard deviation?
solution:
**Given:**

Mean of 100 observation = 40

The standard deviation of 100 observation = 5.1

One observation is taken as 50 instead of 40

**Formula Used:**

Mean(overline x) = (Sumspace of space obsvatiom)/(Totalspace numberspace of space observation)

(Standardspace deviation)² = (sum x_i²)/(n)-(overline x)²

**Calculation:**

⇒ overline x=(1)/(n)sumᵢ₌₁¹⁰⁰ x_i

⇒ sumᵢ₌₁¹⁰⁰ x_i=overline x × n = 40 x 100 = 4000

⇒ (S.D)²=(sum x_i²)/(n)-overline x

sum x_i²=n[(S.D)²+(overline x)²] = 100 × [5.1² + 40²} = 100 × (26.01 + 1600) = 162601

Corrected mean=(1)/(n)sumᵢ₌₁¹⁰⁰ x_i = 4000 - 50 + 40 = 3990

Corrected sum x_i² = 162601 - 50² + 40² = 161701

Corrected mean = (Sumspace of space obsvatiom)/(Totalspace numberspace of space observation)=(3990)/(100) = 39.9

Corrected S.D² = (sum x_i²)/(n)-(overline x)²=(161701)/(100)-39.9² = 25

S.D = sqrt{25} = 5

**Hence, The Correct mean and correct deviation are 39.9 and 5**
